transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Capital One Saver Card.
Earn unlimited 3% cash back on dining and entertainment.
Capital One. What's in your wallet?
Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
Candidates running in key gubernatorial and congressional races.
NPR's Stephen Fowler has more on their closing messages.
President Trump will return this week to Texas and Ohio.
Two of the most high-profile, expensive, must-win Senate races in the country.
Plus, make stops in Florida and Mississippi.
States where he won by comfortable margins in 2024,
but are more competitive because of Trump's unpopular second-term agenda.
And after rallies this weekend in Ohio and Michigan,
Obama heads to Georgia later this week
to rally folks for a governor's race that is expected to be close
and a Senate race that started out competitive but has tilted towards the Democrats.
Still to come, news of where Trump and other high-profile politicians
will spend their final days before polls close November 3rd.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Atlanta.
A panel of federal appeals court judges is questioning the Justice Department's demand
that California election officials set aside thousands of mail-in ballots.
The Trump administration says it suspects the ballots may be from non-citizens
Over the weekend, two of the three judges appeared skeptical of the lawsuit
brought by the Trump administration.
The suit accuses California officials of failing to meet a deadline
to review 20,000 names alleged to be non-citizens.
Saudi Arabia has sent a senior prince to Iran to meet with officials there.
Saudi Arabia says the meeting is aimed at keeping a channel of communication open
to prevent a return to military escalation.
And Piers-Eba Trawi has more.
Saudi Arabia says Defense Minister Prince Khaled bin Salman is in Iran today
for talks on how to de-escalate tensions and achieve regional security.
Iran's state media says the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council
met the Saudi prince and that the meeting also included Pakistan's army chief
and Turkey's intelligence chief.
The visit by Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials to Iran
comes as NPR reports the U.S. and Israel are drawing plans
for a possible large-scale attack on Iran soon.
Iran has vowed powerful counter-attacks in the Gulf.
Already, Saudi Arabia is struggling to defend against attacks
by the Houthis in Yemen, who are backed by Iran.
Egypt's parliament approved a motion to deploy
Egyptian troops to Saudi Arabia to boost its defense.
Aya Bultrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Policymakers from the Federal Reserve begin a two-day meeting in Washington this week.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on some of the economic data the Fed will be tracking.
The Commerce Department will issue its report card on inflation later this week,
a measure that's closely watched by the Federal Reserve.
Prices have been climbing faster than the central bank would like,
but Fed policymakers are expected to hold their benchmark interest rates steady
when they meet on Wednesday.
Oil prices have inched down from recent highs.
AAA says the average price of gasoline has fallen by about a penny a gallon in the last week,
while the average price of diesel fuel has increased about three cents.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
U.S. stocks climbed today.
The S&P 500 rose seven-tenths of a percent.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees or 27 percent of its global workforce.
It comes as the software giant spends heavily on A.I.
The company had about 223,000 full-time employees at the end of June,
shares of Microsoft hit an all-time high this month.
Brazilians have voted to return incumbent president Luis Inacio Lula da Silva to office.
He defeated challenger Flavio Bolsonaro by more than four million votes.
NPR's Kerry Conn reports Bolsonaro is refusing to accept the result.
Polls had predicted Lula, who turns 81 Tuesday, would lose to conservative Flavio Bolsonaro.
The 45-year-old senator is the son of Lula's chief rival, former president Jair Bolsonaro,
who's serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup.
Speaking to supporters last night, a horse Lula thanked Brazilians.
I got this. You know, nothing bad.
Thanks to the generosity of the Brazilian youth who took to the streets to defend democracy, he said.
Bolsonaro is questioning a Supreme Court ruling that allowed polls to stay open two additional hours
and said the justice who ordered the extension, quote, "changed the rules" in the middle of the game.
Kerry Conn, NPR News, Brasilia.
A historic ocean liner is a step closer to becoming the world's largest artificial reef.
Officials in Okaloosa County, Florida expect to sink the SS United States off the Gulf Coast next month.
The vessel will be submerged about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin.
The nearly 1,000-foot ship set a transatlantic speed record on its maiden voyage in 1952.
This is NPR News.
And get NPR+ at plus.npr.org. That's plus.npr.org.

Federal appeals judges skeptical of Justice Department demand that California set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots
Saudi defense minister Prince Khaled bin Salman visits Iran for regional de-escalation talks
Egypt's parliament approves sending troops to Saudi Arabia to boost its defenses
Federal Reserve begins two-day meeting; inflation report due and rates expected to hold steady
Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees amid heavy AI spending
Brazil's Lula wins reelection over Flavio Bolsonaro; Bolsonaro refuses to accept result
Okaloosa County, Florida to sink historic ocean liner SS United States as artificial reef next month
